bearings.paper_claim: Thm 4: an alpha-approximate adaptive greedy gets at least (1 - e^{-l/(alpha k)}) of the best policy; alpha=1 and l=k give 1-1/e. Thm 9: for general instances no polynomial algorithm with budget beta*k approximates the optimum within O(|E|^{1-eps/beta}) unless PH = Sigma2P, even for pointwise linear f.
bearings.paper_location: Thm 4 p.5 (text lines 265-276); Thm 9 p.9 (text lines 737-741)
bearings.system_side: optimize.py runs a heap-based lazy greedy over INC increments (default INC=500). In a fixed stance state the objective is separable with verified concave chunks, giving an exact grid optimum. If a modeled money conversion is reachable the guarantee kind is 'none'. The Golovin-Krause data-dependent bound is labelled 'JAIR'11 Lemma 5.3 / A.9' at line 108.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Thm 4 needs an adaptive monotone and adaptive submodular objective. The fixed-state case is stronger than the paper because it is separable and concave, so the paper adds nothing there. Lemma 5.3 (Adaptive Data Dependent Bound) is in the JAIR text (file 6ba342dad525.txt, line 710) but not in the 13-page CoRR text. A.9 was not located. Thm 9 is worst-case over general instances and does not by itself show that greedy fails on the actual cosponsor instance.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper statements verified verbatim. Softened because the system_side says CELF, which the file never names (it uses heapq lazy evaluation). The rel's inference that Thm 9 explains why no guarantee should be claimed in conversion mode is an inference, not a consequence the theorem states. The code's guarantee kind 'none' is the right conservative behavior.

bearings.paper_claim: An alpha-approximate greedy picks e' with Delta(e') >= (1/alpha) max_e Delta(e). Thm 4 then gives 1 - e^{-1/alpha} at l=k. The full 1-1/e needs alpha=1.
bearings.paper_location: alpha-approximate greedy definition, §4 p.5 (text lines 257-260); Thm 4 (lines 265-276)
bearings.system_side: budgetRecruit picks argmax of g_c, where g_c = (1 - cov[c]) + sum over neighbours PE[c][v](1 - cov[v]). When a target is set, g_c is multiplied by (1 + 2*dT[c]), with dT the max-product proximity to the target (dT[target]=1, values in [0,1]). The multiplier is in [1,3]. The comment claims the classic (1-1/e) of about 0.63 holds.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The weighted rule as written gives alpha=3: if w_c in [1,3] and the chosen c maximises w_c*g_c, then g_chosen >= g_c/3 for every c. The unweighted coverage objective is monotone submodular, so Thm 4 with alpha=3 gives 1 - e^{-1/3} = 0.283. Caveat the rel missed: the candidate pool is pruned (DEG below 0.1 times mean degree, the dropped set, the stanceSafe filter) and the sponsor is forced, so even the untargeted 1-1/e is relative to the pruned pool, not the global optimum.
bearings.verifier_note: Arithmetic checked: 1 - e^{-1/3} = 0.2835. The multiplier and the (1-1/e) comment are verified at the cited lines. The no-target 1-1/e reading holds only over the searched candidate set, which the rel did not mention.

bearings.paper_claim: With additive marginal error eps, greedy gets at least (1 - e^{-l/k}) OPT - l*eps. Thm 6: adaptive seeding under the single-colour independent cascade with any monotone submodular reward is adaptive submodular, giving 1-1/e under myopic or full-adoption feedback.
bearings.paper_location: text after Thm 4, §4 p.5 (lines 340-347); Thm 6, §6 p.7 (lines 512-529)
bearings.system_side: budget_frontier.py runs lazy greedy up to MAXSEEDS=60 with MC=20 replicates and common random numbers. The marginal is max(0, sp - cur)*fac[c]. The seed gate is a CRN draw applied before the cascade. The displayed curve is clamped non-decreasing (prev=max(prev,cur)) and the raw spread is stored alongside it.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Thm 6 covers only the single-colour IC. The two-colour race with anti bystanders and the per-candidate fac weights place the objective outside Thm 6, so no 1-1/e transfers. The eps term is real: Monte Carlo noise over up to 60 seeds enters as -l*eps, and the clamp exists because of observed dips. eps is not bounded anywhere in the code.
bearings.verifier_note: Code facts verified: MC default 20, MAXSEEDS default 60, the clamp, the CRN gate. Paper claims verified. The rel's moderate strength is appropriate.

bearings.paper_claim: Thm 5: with independent location states P[Phi] = product over e of P[Phi(e)] and a monotone submodular base f-hat, the adaptive greedy gets (1-1/e) of the best adaptive policy. Thm 6 covers IC cascades with feedback and does not mention take-up failures.
bearings.paper_location: Thm 5 p.6 (lines 390-401; independence at lines 379-381); Thm 6 p.7 (lines 512-529)
bearings.system_side: gate(n) = max(0.15, seed_prob * SGATE[tier]) in moneyball_core.py. Activation is drawn per member on a CRN stream before the cascade in budget_frontier.py. The allocator does not condition later picks on whether earlier seeds took up the ask.
bearings.transfer_conditions: An adaptive guarantee would need observed take-up between picks, independence across members, and a reward on the realized seed set that is monotone submodular and adaptive submodular. The rel's claim that whip and coalition timing correlate take-up is plausible but not shown by the paper. The SGATE values are unestimated, per the rel. The mapping from sensor failure to take-up is an analogy, not a theorem.
bearings.verifier_note: Thm 5 and the code gate verified. Softened: the rel's statement that an observe-then-replan policy would fall under the guarantee needs the reward to be adaptive submodular, which the rel did not check. The take-up case is not what Thm 5 or Thm 6 covers.

bearings.paper_claim: The expected-spread function of Kempe et al. is submodular (cited in §1 and §6). Thm 4 extends the Nemhauser greedy guarantee to adaptive greedy on true conditional marginals.
bearings.system_side: per_topic_coalition.py computes singleton marginals mg[n] = spread({n}) - base over the top-45 gated candidates, boosts them by (1 + BETA_C*bpf) with BETA_C=0.8, water-fills the dollar budget, then reports the joint spread of the funded set beside the naive-additive sum, noting that spread is submodular.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The allocation uses singleton marginals at the base state, not conditional marginals, so no greedy guarantee transfers to the funded set. Reporting joint spread is consistent with submodularity. The Kempe submodularity claim is verified only as cited background; the Kempe result is not re-derived here.
bearings.verifier_note: Code lines and BETA_C=0.8 confirmed. The paper's treatment of IC spread is cited background and is stated as the paper states it.

bearings.paper_claim: Thm 9 is a worst-case hardness statement for general adaptive stochastic maximization: no polynomial algorithm within O(|E|^{1-eps/beta}) unless PH = Sigma2P, even for pointwise linear f.
bearings.system_side: lt_priming.py sorts candidate recruits by recruit_cost/add (dollars per influence unit) and accepts them against tier thresholds. The code path read makes no approximation claim.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Thm 9 says hard instances exist in the general class. It does not establish hardness for the cosponsor graph. The rel's claim that threshold adoption is not submodular in general is not from this paper and was not checked here.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper statement verified. Code sort verified. The rel's implicit inference that Thm 9 applies to LT priming overreaches, because Thm 9 covers the general class.

summary_issues: Sentence 'Without adaptive submodularity the general problem cannot be approximated within O(|E|^(1-epsilon/beta))' overstates Thm 9. Thm 9 is a worst-case hardness for constructed general instances (puzzle and treasure family), not an if-and-only-if with the absence of adaptive submodularity. Instances without adaptive submodularity can still be easy.

Paul's 'Chen 2023 margin note' that pressure from high-ranking members is not diminishing is unsourced. The item shows n_annots 0, an empty annot_sha12s list and a paul_entries record with no takeaways. Remove it or cite the actual note.
Paul's expectation about GCOMB-style learned policies and his 'static and submodular tier' position are not in any item field and cannot be verified from this item.
'The optimizer runs CELF lazy greedy' is not literally right: optimize.py uses heapq lazy evaluation and never names CELF. Say lazy greedy.
Lemma 5.3 'belongs to the extended JAIR version' is confirmed: Lemma 5.3 (Adaptive Data Dependent Bound) is at line 710 of 6ba342dad525.txt. The A.9 citation was not located and remains unverified.
The '13-page' length is not checkable from the text file, which has no page markers. Treat the manifest page count as unverified.

flags item 'Thm 9 hardness applies, so any greedy (1-1/e) language on cascade-based allocators would be unsupported' overreaches. When Thm 4 stops applying, the honest statement is that the guarantee is unavailable, not that hardness has been shown for that model.

budgetRecruit's untargeted (1-1/e) claim holds only relative to the pruned candidate pool (DEG below 0.1 mean degree, dropped set, stanceSafe) with a forced sponsor. State that scope when repeating the claim.

The summary's 'the paper defines the step the system has not built: seed one member, observe take-up, then re-plan' is an analogy. The paper's observations are item states in a policy tree (sensor states, edge status), not take-up decisions.

The extended-version JAIR metadata (vol 42, pp. 427-486) is external to the text and cannot be confirmed from the 887-line CoRR text. The text itself names only Golovin and Krause (2010), CoRR abs/1003.3967.
